title: Quality-regression protection for hosted endpoints PRD + launch checklist
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Reduce customer-facing quality regressions when deploying model or runtime changes to hosted inference endpoints. This PRD defines automated detection (synthetic + live), canary rollouts, rollback/fallback controls, and launch criteria for the feature set. Goal is to surface regressions early, block large-scale rollouts automatically when quality drops, and provide operators with clear action paths. This covers chat/completions/embeddings/rerank surfaces where behavioral regressions materially affect customer outcomes.
goals: Detect degradations in core quality signals within 30 minutes of a canary rollout
Automatically limit rollout expansion to <5% of traffic when a regression is detected
Provide per-route, per-model quality baselines and automatic comparison against synthetic prompt sets
Reduce severity-1 customer regressions related to model upgrades by 80% vs current baseline over 6 months
Ship a single console page for regression signals with drilldowns and one-click rollback/fallback
non_goals: Fine-grained model-level retraining or tuning (this PRD focuses on serving/runtime controls)
Replacing human judgement for complex semantic regressions—operators can override automated actions
Comprehensive support for every legacy custom endpoint before MVP launch (we will support top 80% traffic surfaces)
Multi-region automated rollback for private deployments in air-gapped environments (out of scope for MVP)
scope: Synthetic evaluation harness: per-endpoint prompt suites + automated score calculation (BLEU/embedding-similarity/LLM eval prompts)
Canary traffic manager: configurable percent slicing, per-customer opt-in/opt-out, and traffic tagging
Automatic regression detectors: rule-based + lightweight ML detectors on metrics (quality_score_delta, embedding-drift, perplexity proxies)
Rollback and fallback actions: pause rollout, revert to previous model version, route to lower-capacity but known-good variant
Console UX: regression dashboard, timeline with events, operator runbook, one-click rollback and escalation links
Alerting and on-call playbook integration: automated pager triggers for high-confidence regressions
Integration with existing evals infra and repo for prompt sets; per-route baseline storage and history
out_of_scope: Automated model retraining loops triggered by regressions
Custom eval authoring UI for non-engineering users (engineers will upload/edit prompt sets via repo)
requirements: R1: Each hosted route must expose a small representative synthetic prompt set (min 50 prompts) stored in repo format
R2: Platform must compute and persist a daily baseline quality score per route+model combination for the last 30 days
R3: Canary scheduler must support: 1%, 5%, 10%, 25% slices and per-tenant targeting
R4: Regression detector must emit a severity and confidence level and must be tunable via feature flags
R5: Rollback action must be executable from Console and via API with audit logs and optional automated rollback triggers
R6: Monitoring must include token-level latency/cost, quality delta, embedding distance distribution, and percentage of flagged responses
R7: Launch must include templates for PM/Support/SE runbooks and customer-facing communication guidelines
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Synthetic eval pipeline computes scores for all supported surfaces (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) and publishes per-route deltas within 30 minutes of a canary change
AC2: Canary rollout can be created via API and Console with percent-slicing and targeting; launch customers can be assigned to slices
AC3: Regression detector triggers an automated pause of rollout and a rollback recommendation when quality drops >8% vs baseline with confidence >= 0.85
AC4: Dashboard surfaces: current canary traffic %, active regressions, top failing prompts, and time-series of quality_score; all queries return <3s for 90th percentile
AC5: One-click rollback executes revert API call, logs event to audit, and restores prior model routing within 60s
AC6: End-to-end test: run a simulated bad model canary, observe detector firing, automatic pause, console alert, and successful rollback in test environment without manual intervention
AC7: Documentation and runbooks reviewed and approved by Support and Solutions Engineering
AC8: No elevated error-rate or >5% latency regression introduced by monitoring/traffic manager in production
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (Internal): Deploy in staging, run synthetic injection tests, verify detector sensitivity using controlled perturbations (2 weeks)
Stage 1 (Beta): Release to 5% of internal beta tenants and Redwood dev orgs, monitor for 2 weeks, collect feedback
Stage 2 (Canary): Open to 1% external canary customers (opt-in) and config for per-customer targeting; require customer opt-in agreement
Stage 3 (Gradual): If no critical regressions for 7 days, expand to 10% then 25% over two weeks, otherwise pause and investigate
Stage 4 (General): Full launch to all hosted endpoints with default detectors enabled; support disabled-by-default for Dedicated MVP customers until separate validation
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to ship: quality_score, quality_score_delta, flagged_response_pct, avg_token_latency, token_cost_per_req, embedding_distance_mean/std, canary_traffic_pct
Dashboards: per-route baseline + live overlay, failing prompt sample table, rolling 1h/24h/7d aggregation views
Alerts: P1 page if quality_score_delta > 10% for 30 minutes or flagged_response_pct > 5% and growing; P2 Slack for lower confidence triggers
On-call playbook: triage steps, rollback steps, escalation matrix and customer communication templates
SLOs: monitoring agent 99th percentile write latency < 2s; alert false-positive rate to be tracked and reduced over first quarter
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High false-positive rate causes unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use multi-signal detectors and require confidence threshold + manual confirmation for major rollouts
Risk: Synthetic prompt sets not representative of customer traffic. Mitigation: require min 50 prompts + periodic augmentation from production signal sampling (anonymized)
Risk: Added telemetry volume increases cost/latency. Mitigation: sample at route level and prioritize high-risk release paths; optimize aggregation windows
Risk: Operator overload from noisy alerts. Mitigation: build suppression rules and aggregate similar alerts; include clear remediation actions in message
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff: alignment on measurable 'quality_score' definition across surfaces (hybrid: embedding-similarity + LLM eval prompts). Action: ENG to prototype scoring modules (ENG-3721)
2025-02-22: Design review: Dashboard wireframes accepted with modifications to show failing prompts and confidence bands (DES-1987). Design flagged need for top-10 failing prompt export
2025-03-04: Decision: automated rollback threshold set at 8% delta with confidence 0.85; manual escalation path preserved for high-risk tenants
2025-03-10: Prototype run: synthetic injection produced a detection within 12 minutes; some noise observed on low-traffic routes—tune plan to require min-sample-size

launch_checklist: 1) Engineering: merge synthetic eval pipeline and baseline persistence into staging cluster
2) Observability: create production dashboards and wire in alerting rules in PagerDuty/Slack
3) Console: add canary creation UI and one-click rollback button; end-to-end e2e tests pass
4) Security/Compliance: review audit logs for rollback actions and retention policy (sign-off from Security)
5) Support/SE: publish runbooks and customer communication templates; run tabletop exercise
6) Beta: enroll internal beta tenants and run 2-week verification plan
7) Telemetry: verify sampling, aggregation and cost impact under simulated 10% canary traffic
8) Product: update docs, release notes, and add feature toggles for early customers
9) Legal/Contracts: ensure opt-in language is present for external canary customers
10) Go/No-Go: cross-functional readiness meeting; accept if AC1-AC8 met and no unresolved P0 blocking issues
